claims.claim: When I walk past the school now, I see the same kids I always saw — the ones who show up early to help the janitor, the ones who pass notes in the back, the ones who ask the question that stops the whole lesson because they actually want to know. The index doesn't see any of that. It sees a number. But I've watched those kids for thirty years, and I know the difference between a kid who can't learn and a kid who hasn't been given a reason to yet. That 6.3 — it doesn't tell you about the girl who reads to her little brother every night because their mom works late, or the boy who fixes the classroom door hinge because he notices it's loose. Those kids are there, all 314 of them, and they're not flat numbers. They're just waiting for someone to see them the way I got to see them.
